Deep Learning-Based Semantic Segmentation of Natural Objects:
A Comparative Study of Baseline Autoencoders and Skip-Connected U-Net Architectures on the Weizmann Dataset
Soumabho Pal, Roll No: 2401AI09, soumabho_2401ai09@iitp.ac.in
Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Indian Institute of Technology Patna
Abstract

This work explores deep learning architectures for dense pixel-level semantic segmentation of natural objects on the benchmark Weizmann Horse Database. A 4-layer Baseline CNN autoencoder is evaluated against a lightweight U-Net featuring horizontal skip connections. Evaluated on 65 unseen test images, the proposed U-Net achieves 85.15% Mean IoU and 91.68% Dice score, delivering an +11.11% IoU improvement over the baseline with sharp boundary reconstruction and minimal parameter overhead.

Introduction
  • Semantic segmentation performs pixel-wise classification essential for autonomous robotic vision, animal monitoring, and natural scene parsing [1].
  • Conventional autoencoders compress inputs into a narrow bottleneck, permanently destroying high-frequency spatial features (slender legs, hooves, tails) [2].
  • Skip-connected U-Net architectures bypass the bottleneck by copying shallow encoder features to the decoder, restoring fine boundary contours without heavy backbones.
Problem Statement
Conventional convolutional autoencoders suffer from severe spatial information bottlenecking during aggressive downsampling, resulting in blurred object boundaries and loss of slender equine limb geometry under complex, camouflaged outdoor backgrounds.
Key Contributions
  • Edge-Preserving Preprocessing: Enforced nearest-neighbor mask interpolation, eliminating floating-point boundary artifacts caused by bilinear resizing.
  • Lightweight U-Net Design: Designed a compact U-Net (467k parameters) that avoids overfitting on moderate-sized datasets (327 images).
  • Quantitative & Real-Time Gain: Attained +11.11% IoU gain (85.15% vs 74.04%) with 128 FPS inference speed on GPU.
Methodology & Proposed Architecture

We formulate an end-to-end lightweight U-Net with DoubleConv blocks [Conv3x3 + BN + ReLU x2] with channel depths 32 → 64 → 128, and horizontal skip connections fusing shallow spatial maps directly into transposed convolutional decoder stages.

Figure 1: Architectural Comparison: Baseline Autoencoder vs Proposed Lightweight U-Net
Algorithm 1: Supervised Semantic Segmentation Training with Adam and BCE with Logits
Require: Dataset D = {(xi, yi)}, Epochs E=100, Batch size B=4, lr η=0.005, Model parameters θ
Ensure: Optimal model weights θ* maximizing validation IoU
1. Partition D into 80% train (262 samples) and 20% test (65 samples) with fixed seed 42.
2. Preprocess images with ImageNet normalization; binarize masks via nearest-neighbor resizing.
3. Initialize Lightweight U-Net with DoubleConv blocks and horizontal skip connections.
4. for epoch = 1 to E do: compute BCEWithLogitsLoss, backpropagate gradients, update weights via Adam.
5. Monitor validation IoU; checkpoint the best model weights θ*.
6. Evaluate test set across IoU, Dice, Pixel Accuracy, and Precision/Recall. Return θ*.

Conclusion
The proposed Lightweight U-Net significantly enhances semantic segmentation accuracy on natural scenes, achieving 85.15% IoU and 91.68% Dice (+11.11% gain), proving that skip connections are indispensable for recovering fine structural equine contours.
